claims.claim_text:
P32 studies a fixed renormalization proposal for the pure genus-two
homology-cover tower
$H_N=\ker(\Gamma\to H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z))$. Physical
lifted time is scaled by exactly $1/N$, and the logarithm of the
raw lift-component product by exactly $1/N^3$. The universal
endpoint asks for recovery of every oriented primitive base-owner
factor. Adversarial review found that the earlier four-package presentation
understated the adverse information already visible in its own
prospective local factors. The present article therefore adopts a
falsification-first architecture. Conditional on a future derivation of
those factors, positive content \texttt{d\textgreater{}1} and zero
content become the first theorem targets; they must be settled before
formal or compact-uniform resources are invested in the exceptional
content-one stratum. The content-one analytic program is now explicitly
contingent and secondary. The project-defined inverse-limit object
\texttt{R\_+}, its localizations and projections, and the separate
zero-content Hahn object remain unresolved constructions. Likewise, any
analytic tail theorem is conditional on survival of the local tests and
would require an absolute logarithmic-summand majorant uniform on each
frozen compact set and compatible with every specified limit order. The
executed work remains literature synthesis over 26 frozen sources and
review-informed argument design. No factor, mismatch, obstruction,
recovery statement, panel, or limit has been proved or computed. All 26
inherited citations retain \texttt{anchor:none}; P32-S13 is
bibliographically \texttt{VERIFIED} but remains background-only, so
claim-to-passage faithfulness is \texttt{INCONCLUSIVE}. Arithmetic A0 remains unavailable, the formal
Route-A tuple is unassigned, positive arithmetic A2 is absent, and Route
B remains closed.
\end{abstract}

Finite-cover products can agree on a selected stratum or finite panel
without recovering every primitive owner. P32 fixes this distinction at
the object level. The base is a marked closed hyperbolic genus-two
surface with unit-speed geodesic flow and presentation

The cover tower is the pure homology tower
\texttt{H\_N=ker(Gamma\ -\textgreater{}\ H\_1(Sigma;Z/NZ))}. It is not
the residual inverse-limit object studied in the preceding branch, and a
conclusion about one tower cannot repair the other. Owners are oriented
primitive surface-group conjugacy classes; inverse classes remain
separately oriented. For an owner with homology vector in
\texttt{Z\^{}4}, content \texttt{d} is the greatest common divisor of
the absolute coordinates, with zero content treated as a separate case.

The normalization is immutable. Physical lifted time is multiplied by
exactly \texttt{1/N}, and the logarithm of the raw lift-component
product is multiplied by exactly \texttt{1/N\^{}3}. Content-dependent
changes, outcome-dependent weights, adaptive schedules, and
favorable-panel selection are prohibited. The universal endpoint
concerns all owner contents, not an average and not the content-one
subproduct alone.

\textbf{Do the prospectively derived local factors for higher-content
and zero-content owners already obstruct the frozen \texttt{1/N} and
\texttt{1/N\^{}3} full-owner recovery scheme; and only if those adverse
tests are survived, what formal and analytic obligations remain for the
content-one subproduct?}

The change is methodological. It does not assert that the candidate
factors are correct or that an obstruction exists. It places the
shortest discriminating theorem targets before the most expensive
formal-topology and compact-uniform program. A higher- or zero-content
obstruction would settle the universal endpoint negatively under the
fixed scheme. Survival would justify continued work. A positive
content-one statement, if eventually proved, would remain a restricted
result.

The article is positioned as a closed-corpus theoretical and
certificate-methods study. Its contribution is the review-adjudicated
ordering of exact obligations: bind owners, derive adverse local
factors, run falsification-first formal comparisons, and only then
develop the contingent content-one branch. No novelty comparison was
authorized, so no priority or originality claim is made.

The word ``owner'' is universal in this article. It never means only a
content-one class. The population comprises oriented primitive
surface-group conjugacy classes across positive higher content, content
one, and the separately typed zero-content case. Inverse classes remain
distinct. This corrects a potentially misleading shorthand in an older
state description and prevents a favorable exceptional stratum from
being substituted for the frozen all-owner endpoint.

Three gates organize the program. The owner gate must bind equality,
oriented conjugacy, maximal roots, inverse handling, serialization, and
prefix completeness to the marked presentation. The local-factor gate
must derive cover order, component multiplicity, primitive-lift status,
rescaled period, and normalized exponent for each relevant content. The
formal/analytic gate must supply the coefficient objects and, if local
tests survive, the uniform tail theorem. A failure at an earlier gate
stops later work; it is not repaired by changing a schedule, selecting a
favorable panel, or moving to a different tower.

The falsification-first order is therefore informational rather than
promotional. It asks the shortest exact questions capable of deciding
the universal proposal while leaving survival, obstruction, and
not-evaluable outcomes all open. The architecture does not infer a
mismatch from the displayed shapes of unproved formulas, and it does not
infer convergence from a finite diagnostic plan.

The required P32 theorem is stronger than the existence of a nearby

summand, uniform on every frozen compact rectangle, compatible with
owner strata, and sufficient for every stated iterated and diagonal
limit. The frozen verification records do not establish that transfer.

Ordered division rings and well-ordered supports, an inverse limit of

All four sources remain background-only. Their resemblance to proposed
constructions cannot define \texttt{R\_+}, its exponent monoid,
transition maps, topology, localizations, or singleton projections. They
also cannot define the separate zero-content Hahn object or validate the
normalization. The frozen comparison \texttt{CP-P32-004} remains
unresolved.

This formal-source boundary is also a truth-condition boundary. A
coefficient comparison has no fixed meaning until the coefficient ring,
support order, transition maps, localization, and projection are all
defined. Resemblance to a known completion or Hahn construction can
motivate a definition but cannot supply it. Consequently, the article
does not report a coefficient mismatch; it reports the construction and
comparison tasks that would make such a statement meaningful.

The executed method is a staged synthesis over frozen literature and
project records. Phase 2 captured 51 records, removed 12 duplicate
manifestations, screened 39 unique records, excluded 13, and retained 26
sources. The inclusion frame covered group algorithms, homology covers,
primitive-orbit products, counting and tails, and formal-topology
precedents. The identity layer classified 25 sources as
\texttt{VERIFIED} and P32-S13 as \texttt{PLAUSIBLE}; 22 inventory rows
are peer-reviewed. The authorized P32-S02 correction fixed its page
range to 287--305. P32-S06 remains a non-peer-reviewed preprint, and
P32-S17 remains bound to its correction-limited support surface.

The evidence matrix retained all 26 IDs and assigned admitted and
excluded claim surfaces. The synthesis grouped them into owner, cover,
product, tail, and formal themes. It did not average away publication
status, correction status, or background-only roles. It also preserved
the distinction between source identity and theorem applicability.

The evidence synthesis was not a vote across papers. Each source-effect
row recorded an admitted contribution, an excluded stronger use, and an
applicability warning. Thus an algorithmic result could inform one
component without being treated as the bound owner interface, and a
cover theorem could provide structural context without proving the
project factor. The same discipline keeps P32-S13 background-only and
keeps the correction-affected claims of P32-S17 outside the admitted
surface.

Citation closure was checked structurally: all source identifiers used
in the manuscript resolve to the frozen 26-row inventory and to exactly
one bibliography entry. This does not verify any theorem passage. Every
use retains \texttt{anchor:none}, no direct quotation is introduced,
and claim-to-passage status remains \texttt{INCONCLUSIVE}. The article
therefore uses the literature to bound a research program, not to claim
that its project-specific factors have already been derived.

Four Phase-5 roles reviewed the exact Phase-4 report: editorial, ethics,
citation integrity, and Devil's Advocate. The integrated result was
\texttt{MAJOR\_REVISION}, with no Critical finding and no ethics
\texttt{BLOCKED} outcome. The author-adjudicated Phase-6 branch requires
a falsification-first narrative. Revision 1 therefore changes the order
and scope of the study, not the mathematical status of its formulas.

The Phase-6 ClaimIntent manifest was frozen before article prose. No new
retrieval, source-finalization call, direct quotation, locator,
experiment, factor computation, coefficient comparison, panel, or limit
was permitted. The executed analytical operation was logical comparison
of frozen definitions and review findings. Every scientific disposition
remains unexecuted or not evaluated.

The higher-content test is ownerwise and target blind. A later execution

be labeled an obstruction. An unresolved projection or factor
derivation returns a not-evaluable state instead.

Survival also has a narrow meaning. If the first registered
higher-content comparison does not yield a mismatch, that result does
not establish the universal scheme, the formula for every owner, or an
infinite product. It licenses only the next predeclared test or proof
obligation. The architecture thereby avoids turning a failed attempt at

claims.claim_text:
The positive-content comparison proposes independent owner variables, a
directed inverse-limit object \texttt{R\_+}, localizations, transition
maps, and finite-support singleton projections. The zero-content
comparison proposes a separate nonnegative-rational Hahn-type object.
The present article does not define these objects by importing a literature
analogy. A valid later construction must state the exponent monoids,
coefficient rings, support conditions, directed maps, topology,
localization domains, and projection compatibility, then prove every
operation used by the factor comparison is well defined.

\texttt{CP-P32-004} remains \texttt{flagged\_unresolved}. Accordingly,
``coefficient mismatch'' is not used as a completed scientific finding.
The local adverse targets are conditional theorem programs whose first
task includes construction of their truth conditions.

For the positive-content object, a later definition must make finite-
support coefficient projections compatible with every transition map.
If localization is used, the denominators and their domains must be
specified before factors are compared. For the zero-content Hahn-type
object, the ordered exponent group and well-ordered support condition
must be stated independently. A map between the two objects cannot be
assumed merely because both contain symbols resembling exponentials.

Singleton projection is central to the falsification-first strategy: it
is intended to isolate one owner without requiring construction of the
whole scalar product. But the projection itself needs a theorem. It
must be defined on the exact completed object, commute with the relevant
transition maps, and preserve the equality notion used in the adverse
comparison. Until those properties close, a visual difference between
two formal expressions has no registered evidentiary force.

Only a surviving content-one formal branch reaches the analytic stage.
The scalar theorem target would need to state exact functions, summation
order, owner exhaustion, modulus schedule, compact domain, and limit
order. The frozen compact rectangles are

The diagnostic prefix \texttt{1\textless{}=k\textless{}=8} and panel
sizes \texttt{m\ in\ \{8,16,32,64,128\}} remain unexecuted and have no
convergence force. A later proof must supply an absolute
logarithmic-summand majorant uniform on each compact, control every
owner stratum used, and justify all iterated and diagonal passages. No
finite grid or favorable prefix can replace those quantifiers.

The order of limits is part of the claim. A theorem for fixed panel size
followed by modulus growth does not automatically imply the reverse
order or the registered diagonal. Likewise, uniformity on sampled
points does not imply uniformity on every compact rectangle. The future
majorant must dominate the exact logarithmic summands independently of
the allowed owner prefix and modulus indices in the stated range, and
its summability must justify every interchange actually claimed.

The factorial and neighboring schedules act as fixed stress paths. They
may not be shortened after an inconvenient content appears, and the
finite prefix through $k=8$ remains only a prospective replay and
serialization diagnostic. No observation on that prefix, even exact,
would establish cofinality, convergence, analytic continuation, or a
limit identity. This keeps numerical or finite symbolic checks in their
proper evidence class.

Eight frozen positions govern the article. First, the algorithmic corpus
supplies separate normal-form, conjugacy, root, list-decision, and
serialization candidates but does not bind
\texttt{SG2OwnerCanonical-v1}. Second, higher-content and zero-content
formulas are adverse local theorem targets conditional on a future
self-contained derivation. Third, the program is falsification-first:
those targets precede formal or compact-uniform investment in content
one.

Fourth, a content-one subproduct is contingent and secondary. Fifth,
\texttt{R\_+}, its localizations and projections, and the separate
zero-content object remain construction obligations because
\texttt{CP-P32-004} is unresolved. Sixth, only after local survival
would the analytic branch require compact-uniform absolute tail control
compatible with every frozen limit order. Seventh, the exact schedules
remain unchanged and finite prefixes remain unexecuted diagnostics.
Eighth, the revision concerns only the pure tower and changes no
scientific recovery or Route status.

These are literature-synthesis and research-design findings. They do not
constitute factor derivations, coefficient certificates, obstruction
theorems, convergence results, or novelty findings.

The present phase is reproducible at the artifact level. The source
inventory, verification rows, Phase-4 report, four Phase-5 reviews,
synthesis, checkpoint, frozen research contract, and ClaimIntent manifest are
hash-bound. The 26 citation IDs close against the 26 references and
verification rows. This does not make the prose generation deterministic
or the theorem transfers passage-verified.

A later scientific interface should freeze producer and verifier roles
before outcomes. The owner layer must bind the exact marked
presentation, equality, oriented conjugacy, maximal roots, inverse
policy, serialization, and prefix completeness. The cover layer must
bind deck action, component count, primitive-lift proof, physical
period, and normalization. The formal layer must bind the positive and
zero-content objects separately. Only after those bindings pass should
the adverse singleton comparisons run.

The smallest next package is therefore not an owner panel or numerical
grid. It is a proof-binding dossier for one higher-content owner and one
zero-content owner selected without target inspection. The dossier
should expose every algebraic premise and return a typed result:
derivation closed and comparison eligible, derivation failed and not
evaluable, or later certified mismatch/survival after separately
authorized scientific execution.

That dossier should be reproducible without access to hidden producer
state. It should include the frozen input and presentation hashes, the
owner certificate, homology vector and content, theorem and schema
versions, deck-action derivation, primitive-lift evidence, normalization
trace, formal-object version, projection proof, verifier receipt, and a
typed disposition. Positive and negative cases should use the same
field contract. Missing evidence should invalidate the comparison
rather than be represented by a default value.

Only after the two local dossiers pass their interface checks would a
population manifest be meaningful. Such a manifest would freeze the
target-blind enumeration rule and exact schedules before any factors are
read. This separation prevents implementation debugging, owner
selection, and scientific interpretation from occurring in one
outcome-dependent loop. None of these dossiers or manifests exists in
the present manuscript.

The falsification-first order changes the value proposition of P32. The
earlier design placed owner binding, lift algebra, formal construction,
and analytic tails in one broad progression. The revised architecture recognizes that
not every package is needed to test the universal claim. If higher or
zero content fails under an exact local-factor theorem, the full-owner
endpoint is settled for the frozen normalization before the content-one
tail problem becomes relevant.

This does not prejudge the outcome. The candidate factors are themselves
unproved, and the formal truth conditions are unfinished. The method
therefore has two early stopping surfaces: failure to derive the factor,
or a later certified adverse comparison. Both are scientifically clearer
than continuing to an infinite product while the local ingredients
remain unresolved.

Content one still has potential value as a restricted analytic object.
Its exceptional status must remain visible. A favorable theorem there
would not erase an ownerwise obstruction elsewhere, and it would not
create arithmetic specificity in a generic homology-cover calibrator.
The pure tower has no intrinsic rational-prime owner map or
\texttt{log\ p} clock in this record.

The Route boundary follows directly. A0 is unavailable, so P32 is not a
primary Hilbert--Pólya dynamics candidate. No stable dynamical
determinant or divisor comparison has been produced, A2--A4 remain
unrun, and no Route-B entry condition exists. A negative local theorem
could still be a meaningful calibration result, but it would not be
Route promotion.

All 26 prose citations retain \texttt{anchor:none}. Source identity and
metadata accounting therefore cannot answer whether a specific theorem
passage supports each transfer. Claim-to-passage faithfulness remains
\texttt{INCONCLUSIVE}, and no locator was invented during revision.

P32-S13 is bibliographically \texttt{VERIFIED} but remains background-only. P32-S06 remains
a non-peer-reviewed preprint whose presentation mapping is unproved.
P32-S17 remains restricted to the correction-unaffected continuation
surface. The formal cluster remains background-only. General retraction
and source-conflict/COI checks remain \texttt{NOT\_CHECKED} and
\texttt{UNKNOWN\_NOT\_CHECKED}.

The core mathematical objects are unresolved.
\texttt{SG2OwnerCanonical-v1} is unbound. The positive- and zero-content
factors are derivation targets. \texttt{R\_+}, its maps and projections,
and the separate zero-content object are not closed constructions. No
compact-uniform majorant or limit theorem exists in the project
artifacts. No diagnostic was run.

The corpus and article also do not establish novelty. The output is
deliberately positioned as a bounded research-program study.
AI-assisted roles used one Codex model family with procedural separation
